questions.subject: COMPUTING_FOUNDATIONS
questions.topic: A loop bound one pass too generous
questions.learningObjective: trace a counting loop whose test includes its own final value
questions.stem: Read this loop and report the value it displays at the end. GUESTS <- 3. greeted <- 0. WHILE greeted <= GUESTS { greeted <- greeted + 1 } DISPLAY greeted.

options.text: 4, because the test still passes on the pass where greeted equals GUESTS
3, because a while loop asks its test before it runs the body
options.misconception: believes the loop stops as soon as greeted reaches GUESTS

options.text: 5, because the counter takes one more step than there are guests
options.misconception: counts an extra pass beyond the one the test allows

options.text: 2, because the first pass is spent setting the counter rather than counting
options.misconception: believes the first pass cannot count towards the total

questions.explanation: The test is written with the same sign as the bound, so it passes while greeted is 0, 1, 2 and 3 and the body runs four times, leaving greeted at 4. A loop that must cover a count needs a strict test, because the strict form stops as soon as greeted reaches GUESTS. A student who reads the wider form as the strict one gets the right answer for the wrong reason, and a student who counts a fifth pass is adding a step the test never allowed.
questions.hint: Ask how many values of greeted satisfy the test as written.

options.text: 1, because the loop runs once and adds nothing at all
options.misconception: believes a pass that adds nothing still counts as a pass

options.misconception: counts the seed as a third contribution on top of both values

questions.stem: Read this loop and report the value it displays. VALUES <- [4, 8, 6]. total <- 0. FOR EACH v IN VALUES { total <- 0. total <- total + v } DISPLAY total.

options.misconception: believes the assignment inside the body has no effect

options.misconception: believes the total is returned to its seed after each addition

options.misconception: believes the last pass only clears and never adds

questions.learningObjective: trace a loop where a variable read on one pass is written on another
questions.stem: Read this loop and report the value it displays. VALUES <- [4, 0, 7]. total <- 0. carry <- 0. FOR EACH v IN VALUES { total <- total + v + carry. IF v > 0 THEN carry <- v } DISPLAY total.

11, because carry is still 0 on every pass and only the values are added
options.misconception: believes carry is never written before it is read

options.text: 22, because the last positive value is counted again on the final pass
options.misconception: counts the final carry a second time on top of the pass that wrote it

options.text: 15, because the zero is dropped but the carry from the first pass is kept
options.misconception: drops the zero value while still crediting the carry it wrote

The 11 comes from treating carry as a permanent zero, which is the natural reading until you notice the value is written inside the loop at all.

4 and 11, because neither variable was ever given a value of its own

options.misconception: believes the subtraction on the second line destroys the saved x

questions.stem: Read these nested loops and report the value they display. total <- 0. FOR i FROM 1 TO 4 { FOR j FROM 1 TO i { total <- total + i * j } } DISPLAY total.

100, because the inner loop runs its full four passes on every outer pass

options.text: 20, because the inner loop stops one short of the outer value each time
options.misconception: believes the inner bound is the outer value minus one

[5, 8, 3], because the loop ends as soon as the value 2 is removed

options.text: [8, 3], because the value 2 is removed and the index then passes the end
